resources.string: Signed with a leaked or public system key

This app is signed with one of Android\'s public test keys or a phone maker\'s leaked system key, and it did not come from Google Play or the phone maker\'s own store. Malware is signed this way to pose as part of the system. Unless you know exactly where it comes from, uninstall it.
Signed with a leaked system key

This app is signed with a phone maker\'s system key that leaked in 2022. It came from Google Play, the maker\'s own store or the phone\'s own setup, and the maker still signs its apps with that key, so this alone is not a sign of malware.
This phone\'s system key is public

The key that signs this phone\'s system is one of Android\'s public test keys. Anyone can sign an app with it, and the phone then treats that app as part of the system. Certified phones never ship this way; custom systems sometimes do.
This phone\'s system key has leaked

The key that signs this phone\'s system is on Google\'s 2022 list of phone makers\' keys that were used to sign malware, and the maker still uses it. An app signed with it can pose as an update of a preinstalled app and keep that app\'s rights; up to Android 14 it can also run as the system. Install apps only from Google Play and the phone maker\'s own store.
This system is signed with Google\'s key for test phones and emulators, not with a phone maker\'s key for phones that are sold.
Signed with this phone\'s system key: the phone\'s maker shipped or approved this app with system rights. It may still contain another company\'s code. The phone reports its maker as %1$s.
Runs as the system user, with the rights of Android itself.
Part of the phone\'s system image.

Google has revoked a key in this phone\'s hardware check, for example because it leaked. The bootloader and system state that the check reports may be forged.

This phone\'s hardware check is not signed with Google\'s attestation key, so the bootloader and system state that it reports cannot be confirmed. Some makers outside Google\'s programme use their own key; a modified system can also cause this.

Its maker describes it as a way for apps to earn money by letting the maker\'s customers send internet traffic through their users\' phones. When this code is on, other people\'s traffic passes through your phone: websites see it as coming from your internet connection, and it uses your data and battery.
